title: Astronomy — Pictor Nebula

content: Topic: astronomy

About four thousand light-years away from Earth sits the Pictor Nebula. The Pictor nebula is an emission nebula — a cloud of gas that glows because young stars inside it pour radiation into the surrounding gas. Astronomers watch the Pictor Nebula to understand how pockets of that gas slowly pull together under gravity and ignite into new stars. They observe this process with an optical telescope, tuned to red light.

Images of the nebula tend to leave a strong impression, even on people who don't usually pay much attention to astronomy. The colors and shapes seem almost too vivid to be real, though they're exactly what the telescope captures. It's the kind of sight that makes clear why so many people find deep-sky objects captivating.

Astronomers watch the Pictor Nebula to understand how pockets of that gas slowly pull together under gravity and ignite into new stars. That's how new stars form there — gravity slowly pulling the gas together until it ignites.
They observe this process with an optical telescope, tuned to red light. That optical telescope specifically takes in red light, the frequency at which the nebula's gases shine most intensely.

About four thousand light-years away from Earth sits the Pictor Nebula. Spectroscopic analysis shows elevated carbon and nitrogen relative to hydrogen, consistent with material dredged up from the star's core in its final years. The shell is expanding outward at roughly twelve kilometers per second, slow enough that it should fully disperse within about ten thousand years.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describe the Pictor Nebula? Select all that apply.

options.1: It is a cloud of gas
options.2: It is located about four thousand light-years from Earth
options.3: It is lit from within by young stars
options.4: It is a dense ball of old stars

questions.question: How do scientists observe the Pictor Nebula? Select all that apply.

options.1: With an optical telescope
options.2: By picking up red light emitted by the nebula
options.3: Using radio equipment that picks up regular pulses
options.4: By measuring how its mass varies over time

questions.question: What do astronomers study the Pictor Nebula to learn? Select all that apply.

options.1: How gravity pulls pockets of gas together
options.2: How gas clouds ignite into new stars
options.3: How gravitational waves ripple through a region of space
options.4: How black hole emissions change

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Pictor Nebula? Select all that apply.

options.1: A gas cloud lit by embedded young stars that is studied to understand how new stars form
options.2: A gas cloud lit by embedded young stars that is studied to understand gravitational waves
options.3: The remains of a dying star that is studied to understand how new stars form
options.4: The remains of a dying star that is studied to understand gravitational waves

questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies what the Pictor Nebula is? Select all that apply.

options.1: An emission nebula — a dense ball of old stars gravitationally bound together
options.2: A globular pulsar — a cloud of gas lit by its own embedded young stars
options.3: A globular pulsar — the collapsed core of an exploded massive star
options.4: An emission nebula — two stars in a close gravitational orbit
